ages.title: Upcoming age milestones

what.40: Long-term care premiums start (no filing needed).
what.60: If pay drops on re-employment after retirement, consider same-day loss and re-acquisition to lower the standard remuneration immediately.
what.65: Long-term care premiums stop (moves to the municipal care insurance; no filing needed).
what.70: Pension coverage ends. No filing if pay is unchanged (handled by the Japan Pension Service); otherwise file the age-70 notification within 5 days.
what.75: Health coverage ends (moves to the late-stage elderly medical system). File the loss of coverage within 5 days. Dependents need to join another plan such as National Health Insurance.

annual.seasonal: This difference occurs every year due to the nature of the work (e.g. busy season)

hint.reflect: Applying saves the standard remuneration from September (reason: annual review) and a record of how it was decided. Existing September entries are not overwritten.

export.title: 1. Export
export.lead: Exports one row per employee per month for employees employed during the selected period. Entered months have numbers and missing months are blank, so the file also works as a template.
export.hint: Encoded as UTF-8 with BOM (opens directly in Excel). Up to 24 months.

import.title: 2. Import
import.lead: After you choose a file, a review screen appears. Nothing is saved until you press Import.
import.partial: Saving failed partway. {{done}} of {{total}} records were saved. Import the same file again to add only the rest (saved records show as unchanged).
import.zeroPadded: For {{n}} rows whose employee number lost its leading zeros, the zeros were restored for matching (Excel can drop them).
import.hasErrors: Some rows have problems, so nothing can be imported. Fix the CSV and choose it again (nothing was saved).
import.nothing: There is nothing to import (all rows match saved records or are blank).
